label: Early copy-phase output of s/t/j/y/g/3/p/r/i/v (strongest at <DEL>)
explanation: Almost entirely an output-phase unit: 97% of activation mass is at t >= L. The <DEL> step alone holds 56% of mass (31% of delimiter steps fire), and the top activations are all at <DEL> or the first one or two copy steps. Firing depends on which token is being output: out_tok in {s,t,j,y,g,3,p,r,i,v} has 3-6x lift. It also rises with outputs remaining (to_go = 8 rate 0.23 vs to_go = 0 rate 0.01), so longer sequences fire more. It is nearly silent during the original phase (rate 0.006, never at t = 0). The predicate (output phase, at least 4 outputs left, out_tok in that set) gets dev F1 0.40 and mass recall 0.58. Plain phase == 1 gets F1 0.38 and mass 0.56. Precision stays low because many delimiter/early-copy steps with these tokens do not fire, and the extra conditioning on sequence content I tried did not fix this.
